notes.title: STEAM SUMMER SALES 2024
notes.content:
Gamers,

We announce the opening of this 'Summer Steam Sales' from RolldBox Games, and we are offering a reduced price so you don't miss out on the world we have created for you, featuring the following NEW UPDATES:

1. The catalog of actions around the Planet. Once the game is completed, the player receives a certificate after executing the selected action:

🍃 Protect 100ft² Of Wildlife Habitat

🐢 Save A Sea Turtle

🌳 Plant a Tree

🏞   Buy 10ft² Of Land For Nature Reserves

🌊 Protect 1000 M² Of Marine Area

💨 Carbon Offset

🪸 Coral Restoration

♻ Clean Ocean Plastic


2. Other improvements:

🧲 Pulse | Temporarily heals the area of the planet you're in, reducing its aggression while you explore and heal it permanently.

✨ Enhanced Colors | The color palette has been enriched to offer a more vibrant and immersive visual experience.

🐠 Addition of Wildlife | Birds, fish, etc., which can become more aggressive towards the player until they are healed.

💚 Evolution of Flora | Carnivorous plants.

🩹 More Abilities with Partial Healing | Expand your repertoire, bringing a new layer of strategy and depth to the survival system.

An ideal game designed for when you get off work so you can play for a while in the evening — you'll benefit from a wellness element as you restore and recover the Planet. It falls under 'Positive Gaming' because you can enjoy watching the entire space being restored, the fauna and flora coming back to life, and the Torek interacting with you. With a wealth of characters and a deep narrative, it's an experience you won't forget.

notes.title: Update of Those Who Came: Healing Solarus !!
notes.content:
Hello Gamers!

We have been able to check the Those Who Came status, and gather some of the issues that might have been affecting you all on your journey through Solarus. From the different issues found and also notified by you, we have been able to address most of them!

We have identified a critical issue that could cause the game to get stuck and force the players to restart the mission, forcing them to go through an unnecessary set of menus and maps.

There was a mission that could be blocked if the players skipped a step by opening a door before being asked, now the mission will keep going if the case is matched.

In addition to this major fix, we have been able to identify a set of more quality of life improvements and issues that were affecting the experience:


 Language typos mostly happening in Spanish and Catalan
 At the start of a mission, an empty dialogue box could appear and never fade
 Certain trees have been relocated and now they are not floating
 Modified map boundaries to properly adjust to the playable pathing
 Visual issue with certain consoles when using the Surface Walker suit
 Visual issue with the energy tubes that they weren’t displayed at the right pace, but all of them at the end of the quest
 Visual issue where certain objects where being occluded and were hardly visible
 Improved the visuals for the healing plants to make it easier to see when is healing
 Adjusted the Torek archives and the batteries to only appear when not obtained 



We hope that with these fixes your experience with Those Who Came: Healing Solarus improves and helps you to reach Bineok. We need to save this world!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/32b903f9034d47313196d353918c27e445a0eea9.png

Also! If you'd like to be posted on the latest news, give us some human tips or just have a chat over coffee then you can always joing our discord server! The invite is just a click away ;)

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/29d4f3762728f54caaf673654ea2d133d3a694ab.gif

Dear human explorers 👽  At Rolldbox Games we are so thrilled to have already developed the Full Version of Those Who Came: Healing Solarus completely. 

This adventure has been so wild and it came plenty with difficult tasks and obstacles to tackle like the most wise Sainen. We have learned so much as a team and as an indie studio, and this can only translate into pouring out there amazing titles which we hope you’d be eager and happy to live out intensely. The adventure has not ended!

Most of all, we are thrilled for you to play it already! We can’t wait for your feedback, kind reviews and support as a gaming community. 

[previewyoutube=EfCChCi0s-Q;full][/previewyoutube]

Much has happened since the Early Access and we will never forget all the help we received in the community; from the suggestions, feedback and contributions that arrived to us to streamers, indie fellows and publishers that were happy to comment their perspective. 

Now it is about time to enjoy the story of the Sainen and Solarus completely. We hope you enjoy playing it as much as we did developing it, with all the care we best know how to deliver.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/08aadd5da2752324ba62ab382ee3969882f21b6b.gif

Those who Came is a sci-fi cooperative adventure with some touch of RPG, where you will have to work as a team to survive and thrive on a hostile planet. Players must evade an astounding combination of challenges and environmental menaces, requiring lateral thinking, communication and, most importantly, cooperation! If you dare to play alone, you can! Be open to learn and master the different energies to move around!

It is all about healing instead of killing!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/3a6554907109507e245f1429f0044778847a122e.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/2027a71c03f5313b46cc623c18c86f3bba982f86.png

 4 energies to move around Solarus: Choose your own style by using the energy with the different shapers: Airy, Ether, Fire and Jointer.
 Play either alone or along with your friends, up to 4!  into a campaign with plenty of challenges to stop Bineok and his experiment.
 Explore and find the different suits to interact with the world and restore life in Solarus to turn it into your new home.
 The more you heal, the better it gets. By caring for the planet, you will be able to face the final challenge with some advantages.
 Dive into our Arcade mode, where you can face your friends in competitive PVP arenas. Harness the versatility of all 4 energies using them creatively on other players.


Remember, if you are a press writer or a streamer and you want to play Those Who Came: Healing Solarus for a review or stream, you can always contact us through our social media at @rolldboxgames or our Discord Channel! We can provide you with a key and a juicy presskit we’ve been crafting these weeks. Don’t hesitate to ask!

Happy gaming!

notes.title: Solaru’s Inhabitants: The Torek
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/d79249ac21e00818648a89c0bb5a2d0d20bef6e3.jpg


Hello again fellow explorers, here we are with another chapter of your training as a Sainen pioneer amidst the thrilling lands of Solarus. In today’s masterclass we are going to discuss the nature of Solarus' fellow inhabitants, the Torek. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/fc3e17be8bdde91fc280771d8ab6faf6c6c4119a.png

The Torek are descendants of what humans call “Lizards”, a common creature in the Universe. In this case though, they have evolved until they became a civilization type I in Kardashev’s Scale. They are a bit more advanced than our human neighbors, but a lot less than us, the Sainen. We belong to type III!

All Torek look very similar to each other, and while there is not much difference between them, they have completely different attitudes towards us! Let’s see:


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/f3eea8dc359f75526fc09207000bed97207aa182.gif


Friendly Torek

You may bump into them from time to time. They sport a friendly attitude because deep down they know you come in peace and want to restore life in their home planet. As a consequence, they will try to bring you aid in the form of goods or information. Kolra, an important character among the Torek, or Commander Toan, in charge of Torek’s operations, fall into this category and will accompany you in your journey.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/441141e53636dbdb95b324015f461197386741f1.gif


Vendors 

They are inherently good and will exchange money or resources with you. In future versions of Those Who Came, they will be key for your missions since they have valuable information about the new planet you are exploring. You will be able to obtain new suits, technology or important items in your missions thanks to their help.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/1e57481ed3a09e97893de5ff52ee6e4c3eceb9b1.gif


The Guardians of Solarus

These Torek have seen the worst in their homeland while being in touch with the corruption ravaging planet Solarus. As a result, they have suffered a lot and won’t hesitate attacking you when they consider you’ve approached an object, structure or important element they are guarding. They look at Sainen as another potential threat that could destroy them. 

This group of Toreks are broad and some of them will throw different attacks towards you. Even though their attacks are usually defensive or indirect and will just sabotage your purpose, here are some hints to get your crew prepared:


 Area Guarding
The Torek will create a round area in front of them. If they catch you inside this area your Suit Shield will get damaged and your life will be compromised! Please, check your life bar placed in the lower left corner of your screen if you are caught in this situation. 

 Dart Guarding
Some Torek have a bracelet equipped with darts that provoke our movements to be half time slower than originally, it would seem you had consumed one of those human beverages drunk at parties on Earth. We know you would not! Just avoid this situation, explorer!

 Trap Guarding
Just beside the Dart Guardians, there are some Torek that like to persecute and catch you in their arms. They don’t want to kill you, they just try to avoid you entering places “you shouldn’t be in” by propelling you outside that zone once they’ve put their broad hands all over. 



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/b8071e37032cd3e1eda341580804e20af0af0ac6.gif


As you can see, Torek come in all forms and sizes, but their key to know what’s their deal is actually paying attention to their actions! 

Which of these Torek guarding techniques will be more challenging to you? Tell us in the comment section, or join our Discord community today.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/7c2e73b9eb046815d27c28631cc2a6f26647ec2d.png

Happy gaming!

notes.title: Those Who Came Major Update !
notes.content:
Greetings, fellow explorers! 

Today is a big day for Those Who Came. We are proud to announce our biggest update to date, a work that comes with several fixed issues and the introduction of a New Tutorial System to guide you through your first steps as a Sainen, among other juicy perks.  


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/979cc244a7a3eaf39a6cebe3a6b59ba997d1c667.png


Thanks to this much needed guidance, you will be learning to choose between Energies and know how to use them with the Shapers way faster and easier than in our previous update. Do not forget that the suit you wear is your battery and the source of your abilities. Charge your suit by absorbing energy from the environment and choose among the four Energies–Firei, Ether, Airy and Jointer–the one most attuned to you. The Shapers will enable you to leverage your energy for maximum effectiveness. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/13c43d559d9af0145dbebd6d382397721decba84.png


February 25th Update Features:

 We have added the second configuration of the Jointer: Jointer Mimic !
 The Energy System has been reduced to 10 levels. You will learn the second configuration of your Energy when reaching said level.
 Onboarding experience improved, as well as the Energy introductory levels, we highly recommend to replay the maps !
 These maps now contain a speedrun timer to see who is the fastest Sainen in the Galaxy!



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/6481b5f86bbc29f5e90cb7e48a9bbeaabbd6986e.png


February 25th Update Fixes:

 Fixed many issues related to the Mission System
 Translation related text mistakes fixed
 Cave Expedition issues fixed
 Navigation issues found in the game maps fixed 
 Issues with the color outlines related to energies solved
 Errors with the Steam icons when playing online resolved



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/9a03be7197591e1e60ff61608505d1c3d1ff39ca.png


Additional changes:

 The Quest Target icon has been changed for visibility purposes
 Improved navigation pathings on the caves for the last puzzles



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/c69d063c1d50e499c09ce8157a5c0c84b627f181.png


As Those Who Came nears its full release, some optional gameplay features will come out of the game to be refreshed and optimized for future post-launch updates while other exciting features will be introduced at launch for the first time. So stay tuned! 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/d2e8c4bee931da959f72b676989941f5616d6f47.png


Said that, we can’t wait to see you play our latest version of Those Who Came! Do you have any feedback? Tell us in the comment section, or join our Discord community today.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/7c2e73b9eb046815d27c28631cc2a6f26647ec2d.png


Happy gaming!

notes.title: The Stadium, a PvP Guide.
notes.content:
For some Sainen, overlapping expeditions may be hard. Not everything is about duty! And certainly, most of the crew need both a break from their missions and a training space built specifically to unravel their most recently acquired abilities. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/44bf70022ea8b3ce81bdb7f1e0928b98dd60b3ea.gif


This is why Sainen’s top pioneers have access to The Stadium, an area in which they can compete against each other by building two teams. The objective? Storing a huge amount of super valuable energy in your team’s battery before your competitors fill in theirs. The crew members that have stored the most energy win the match! 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/12373ed281287dd83c8bfc8b1e7b69fdd6b0c13e.gif


Of course, this comes with some fun challenges, like preventing your counterparts from gathering energy, preparing obstacles and overall sabotaging their objective in a hilarious manner, the Sainen style. Of course, all of this will happen quickly the more you have previously mastered your preferred abilities! 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/0330c41dd40150995b7353cbaeb87d26bfa33884.gif


Here’s a brief guide on how to start your PvP match with your crew:

 Both teams must be in the same region in order to play.
 Teams can be set by couples against couples, 3vs3, and 4vs4.
 Each member of your team and the opposite must have clicked on the PvP mode.



{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/f73d902f9ed8372394011134d22d73ce0e565e4d.gif


Remember! You can still receive damage from the threatening environment, but not directly from your counterparts, so do not get mistaken: these are not The Hunger Games! Or are they?

Said that, we can’t wait to see you play. Are you more into missions or this cute PvP mode? Tell us in the comment section, or join our Discord community today.

Happy gaming! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/7c2e73b9eb046815d27c28631cc2a6f26647ec2d.png

notes.title: Hot fixes and new features
notes.content:
Hot fixes and new features of 0.7.14.8 version

After X-MASS major update of December 9th, we continue developing and improving things by listening to the community.
Thanks for all the feedback received and enjoy playing this Christmas Holidays with all these new elements!


[Features]

•	User Interface adaptation: We have changed the position of the layout for the suit interface, ensuring a better comprehension of the gameplay capabilities, also adding the player HUD with extra information about their teammates.
•	Now you can see your and your team Steam icons in the UI.
•	PvP Gameplay modified: we have simplified the game experience to make it smoother and leave more room to develop the synergies between energies and teams.
•	We have adjusted the speed of the Jointer ball: Now jointers can chase down any speedy teammate to ensure that they don’t become blocked because of the ball pursuing another player.
•	Now destroyable rocks by Firei can be crossed from the moment they have been destroyed, not after they fully glow.
•	Added new health dropables in the caves helping the players to outrun the threats of Solarus.
•	New tutorial messages for the main mechanics and features added to ensure that the basics are understood properly. 


[Fixes]

•	Fixed issue that prevented some achievements from being accomplishable.
•	Fixed several missions from Solarus Surface.
•	Fixed economy issues related to obtaining new mods and suits.
•	Fixed vendors to let them sell specific products from day or night.
•	Solved visual element issues with minor resolutions and quality settings.
•	Modified quest objective visuals for better performance.
•	General improvements on game performance focused specifically on the Surface of Solarus.
•	Solved visual displays on the dialogues.
•	Improved infrastructures over the surface for a better experience playing expeditions.
•	Fixed issue with the quest log that didn’t display when needed.
•	Fixed issues with quest targets that remained in the world after completing the quest.
•	Fixed issues with the energies video showcases.
•	Cinematics now mute all the game when running, preventing an issue of hearing world elements while playing them.
•	The Commander Artissa now does not block in the tutorial pathing, ensuring she reaches the end no matter what the player does.
•	Solved an issue in the HERMAION ship that prevented the player from leaving the area the first time.
•	Solved an issue that prevented some players from binding themselves to a certain energy.
•	Improved performance of the loading screen, ensuring that it disappears at the correct moment letting the player play from moment 0.
•	Fixed issue with Toreks at caves that didn’t appear properly.
•	Fixed issue that forced players to see the introduction at the personal ship every time they entered.
•	Fixed issue that didn’t update properly each player when reaching their personal ship, forcing them to reload the game to see their true progression.
•	Fixed issue in the last Solarus Surface mission that sent players back to the spaceship where they could not start any new mission.
•	Fixed an issue in the Firei binding level, where players could die and had to restart the game.
•	Modified some gameplay elements in the Caves that made players feel dizzy about what to do or how.


[Other changes]

•	Fixed some issues with navigation elements.
•	Added sounds on the proper surfaces that weren’t set accordingly.
•	Fixed some sounds that weren’t binded to “Sound configurations”.
•	General improvements on the visuals of the surface, giving a better perception of the day/night.
•	Changed size of the searching display to ensure each text is readable.
•	General improvements on text translations.
•	Adjusted some visual elements related to interactable objects with proper outlines and colors.
•	Prevented the Shade of torek from disappearing when he had talked to players.
•	Fixed Sainen ship minor navigation issues that prevented some players from moving around.
•	Fixed suit textures that were shown incorrectly.
•	Fixed an issue in the Stadium “Learning the basics” that forced the player to play without their equipment.
•	Adjusted some items over the Solarus Surface that weren’t placed properly.
•	Fixed minor issues over the Energy binding levels that created confusion in the gameplay and added minor helpers.


[Images of new User Interface]

notes.title: The X-Mass update is now live!!
notes.content:
Good day, explorers:

Our first major update, code-named 'X-Mass', is now live on Steam. As we revealed to you last week, it comes with very relevant changes in the way the Sainen abilities are introduced to players, new areas of Solarus to explore, and new ways of enjoying the experience both with friends and on your own. Also, the story of Solarus and the Sainen has been updated, with a lot of surprises for you to discover! There's a new trailer to celebrate this update, you can check below these lines.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/ce6fc7a05e052ec77afa4fb2fac49fafebc63bc0.jpg

This is a major milestone for us, as Those Who Came is beginning to take the shape we envisioned back in the day. We have been working extra hard these last weeks to ensure that the X-MASS update was ready before Christmas, so you and your friends have time to experience the game during your holidays.

If you are new to Those Who Came, you should be aware that we will live stream the game here on Steam at 12:30PM and 16:30PM (both CET). We will show the new mechanics featured in this update as well as the new maps and other quality of life improvements.

For more news, updates, or a friendly chat about the game, we invite you to follow and join the conversations here on the Steam forums, our community on Discord, and our social media channels: Twitter, Instagram, and Reddit.

Happy gaming!

notes.title: X-MASS update coming on December 9th
notes.content:
Morning, explorers,

As we told you on Twitter last Friday, we are very happy to announce that the next major update for Those Who Came is about to be released. 

The update will hit Steam on December 9th with more content, technical improvements to the game's core features and much more. We truly believe this is a significant leap forward compared to previous builds, and one that puts us closer to our vision for Those Who Came. 

With this new update, we have made some changes to our roadmap, you can check them below.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/897d5fcd308117a21597f6152a386c4aca88971b.jpg

Among the new features, we have renamed some mechanics, and introduced some slight changes in the number of players that will be needed to complete some tasks. We have also tweaked the party system to create a more seamless experience, added new maps and did a ton of bug fixing.

Let's spell the changes out part by part!


Adapting the terminology
Science fiction transports players to futuristic contexts — often far removed from their own in both space and time — where scientific and technological innovations define everything. In contrast to fantasy works, here unlikely events must have a logical and rational basis. For this very reason, we understand that words like "magic", or “spells”, don’t fit a story like ours. Therefore, the upcoming patch will rename the elemental abilities of the Sainen: from now on, we’ll always refer to them as “Energies”.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/5cb4f3acc8fbff9042e5bb3136c5779b241e05a8.jpg

In this sci-fi context, the devices used by the Sainen to catalyze these energies of the Universe will be called “Shapers”, not “magic props”; and each player will be able to set four types of configuration depending on the ability we need to use.

Also, for the sake of consistency, the way in which the chosen shaper is configured will be called “configuration” instead of the previous “spell”.


Tweaked energies
The Sainen, as an advanced civilization, are capable of handling special energies that serve them as a way to interact with the environment in many different ways. 

There are 4 different types of energies, all related to a specific element:


 Airy: Levitation. Creates energy flows that make the player ascend and be able to access unreachable areas. It also prevents them from big falls. 
 Firei: Glowing Orb. The Firei energy becomes a light in the darkness, and can melt down certain objects. 
 Ether: Shade. Ether gives the players the ability to reshape themselves or other objects. This is useful to go through walls and strong structures to reach new areas.
 Jointer: Object transmutation. Jointer empowers your companions and creates new paths by energizing the environment.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/1733b23d6d48156cac39b3b4d72f61fa6bfae65e.jpg

In order to use the energies, each Sainen will first need to establish a link with the ability they want to master, and will have the option to practice in a tutorial level specifically designed for this purpose. Your kind has awakened after a long period of time, and will need to start all over again from scratch; thus, you will begin learning any ability from the basic level.

During your mission on planet Solarus, you will find some energy spikes to capture and get some “configurations”; that is, the way to set up the devices -”Shapers”- to generate the energies.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/36fcf0db775b2828d843dd7f49e88b73e98abe84.jpg

The energy skill levels range from 1 to 50, which is the highest. As you level up, using the energies will become increasingly difficult, even much more if you are trying to excel in all of them. Playing with friends means that each of your companions can specialize in one or two of these energies, depending on the number of players. However, it is also possible for only one player to master all of them -it’s extremely challenging, but achievable!


Multiplayer experience
Those Who Came is a multiplayer game. We recommend that you gather 4 friends to be able to enjoy the whole experience, but there are several missions that can be played in Single player mode, and others that will require a minimum of 2 players. For the last missions you may need all the 4 to complete the adventure. We have tweaked this number as before there were some missions that needed up to 7 players to be completed.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/5f82743d02937d2774478b60f50ac7abc2a86efa.jpg

Remember that as a crew, you have access to a PvP area called The Stadium that can only be enjoyed in multiplayer mode. It is a very exciting place where you can upgrade your equipment, earn Halis, and test your skills with the energy you have gathered -not individually, but with your friends! PvP can be played in two groups of 2, the minimum required, two groups of 3, or two groups of 4. There are several options for two different parties to play together, and have fun while mastering their energies!


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/fad235802b2095c44034bd0ac227a6aae4fa62bd.jpg


New maps
Along their journey, the Sainen will have to learn about Solarus, the planet that is meant to be their new home: its surface, its environment, its fauna and flora, and how to establish contact with the natives. Solarus also changes its behaviour depending on the day and night cycles! 

The next update will bring some very interesting new areas to the map. For example, the Torek’s Cave, an unknown part of the planet with some environmental peculiarities, where the native inhabitants of the planet, the Torek, are surprisingly able to live. The Sainen will need to discover Solarus and its possibilities through the different missions; it’s a vast planet with many areas to explore, so it won’t be an easy task!


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/ca1e641d601c313e46cf744d4982b403831f2d7f.jpg

All these new places will help the Sainen to understand more about Solarus' history, and discover relevant elements that will have a key impact on how to heal the planet and make it fit to live in. 


Characters
The update of Dec 9th will also bring new names to certain elements and characters in the story. We have been thinking on how some of them could be improved to better fit the story and the world we have created. With this in mind, we decided to rename some of them; the most remarkable changes are the name of the Sainen Commander, who we will call Artissa from now on, and the main ship, HERMAION.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/4d73ab66d2f2e463ee0d0fd05e592734f7c74bee.jpg

Another important decision has been to discard all characters’ voices. We realised that too many new recordings would be needed, as the number of NPCs with dialogues we had originally planned to include in the story had increased considerably. Instead, we will use very brief sounds to identify the speaker, and will most likely review sounds and voices thoroughly in upcoming updates. 


Bug fixing and QoL improvements
We have also added some hotfixes to this new update. Regarding our party system, for instance, we have solved several bugs in order to improve performance and stability, while including several quality of life improvements. Besides, as usual with a new update, we have polished the build to remove bugs. 




Here are all the things to look forward to on Dec 9th! 

For more news, updates, or a friendly chat about the game, we invite you to follow and join the conversations here on the Steam forums, our community on Discord, and our social media channels, Twitter, Instagram and Reddit.

Take care and have a great week!

notes.title: Nominate Those Who Came for the Steam Awards!
notes.content:
Greetings, explorer:

You arrived just in time! The 2021 Steam Awards are here and we're super excited about joining the celebration this year — and even reaching a prominent position amongst other similar games! But this is something we can't do on our own, you know. We need your support to make it possible. As the multiplayer mode is an essential feature to foster cooperation between players, we would love to be featured in the Better With Friends category.

If this is your first time learning about Those Who Came, we invite you to check our store page and our FAQ section:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1708570/Those_who_Came/

At this point, you may be wondering: “Why do you deserve my vote?”. For us, the reasons are quite obvious!

 First because, as we exposed up there, Those Who Came is entirely focused on creating positive gaming experiences based on cooperation. The Sainen, represented by you and other players, will work together with the Torek to make a good place for living out of Solarus.
 Second, because that cooperation also means caring about others' needs and, at the same time, prioritizing the success of each mission. No matter how much you enjoy using a concrete kind of skill, you must be flexible enough to learn many others.
 And third, because we show that such an ambitious goal can be achieved without hurting others — at least, putting physical violence and cultural dominance out of the equation.


Votings have already started. Would you spread the word by sharing your love for the game with your friends and other players before December 1st? It would mean a lot to us. Please, remember that you can only nominate a game in a single category even though a game can receive multiple awards. Let's see how far we can go together!

https://store.steampowered.com/steamawards/#BetterWithFriends

Have fun and stay safe!
Rolldbox Games

notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
notes.content:
Greetings, explorer. If this is your first time checking Those Who Came on Steam, surely you will have a lot of questions. Let’s get started to solve them all!

GENERAL QUESTIONS

First of all, what kind of game is Those Who Came?
We define it as a sci-fi cooperative survival RPG. Players will follow the story of the Sainen, a strong and resilient species that nearly faced extinction after their planet collapsed. Hoping for their kind to survive this cataclysmic event, they sent forth a ship full of explorers frozen in a cryogenic state. You and your friends will become four young survivors called to explore a new planet: Solarus. The planet seems to be in danger, just as yours was, so it’s in the hands of your race, and your local allies, the healing of this land you expect to call “home” someday…

What is the game about?
In each mission, you will explore a new area of Solarus in search of different ways to help the planet: from researching the local vegetation to restoring some destroyed energy facilities. Every action counts, so the most important factor to achieve success is planned cooperation: decide your individual roles as a team, and never leave the rest behind!  

What requirements must my PC meet to run the game under the best conditions?
Our recommended system requirements are:

 OS: Windows 10
 Memory: 16 GB RAM
 Storage: 15 GB available space

To play it under the minimum system requirements you just need:

 OS: Windows 10
 Memory: 8 GB RAM
 Storage: 15 GB available space


When did the development start?
By August 2020, the pandemic really awakened our game developer senses! We explored several ideas and this was the one we liked the most. 

What else should I know about the development process?
Our main work tool was Unreal Engine 4 -- version 4.25.4. Plus, the game is developed with a mix of Blueprints (for environmental artists and game designers), and C++ (programmers). Most of our content is custom-made; we only use plugins to improve the connections to our servers and track data for game improvement.



EARLY ACCESS & FULL GAME VERSIONS

Why Early Access?
When we set out to develop Those Who Came, we wanted to challenge some of the foundations of the RPG genre, like its emphasis on combat. We want to create a refreshing experience, something that feels new and unique. Testing and honing these ideas with real players will allow the game to grow to its true potential.

How long will the game be in EA?
Our goal is to transition to full release during 2022 as soon as we feel the game is content-complete and polished, ensuring an engaging experience for all our players.

How is the full version planned to differ from the EA version?
The full version is planned to include new maps, more creatures, extra suits, and new special powers. The feedback of the community will be a key factor not just to polish these features, but to set the priorities and decide their final shape.

What is the current state of the EA version?
The core mechanics and features of the game are already implemented: you can create teams and add friends, craft and trade goods in cooperation with other players, explore the landing zone on Solarus, and compete at the Stadium in PvP. You can also use the 4 initial special powers, in combination with a varied set of suits and suit mods. We are working hard on balancing, as well as polishing the currently available maps. In terms of stability and performance, the game still has some bugs – but most of them are known and identified, and we are working to iron them out.

Will the game be priced differently during and after EA?
The price will increase on full release as the game receives more content.

Is the game coming to other platforms?
We’d love to ensure that there will be a console version, but Those Who Came is still in Early Access and our priority now is to make a game we can feel proud of.



GAMEPLAY

What kind of missions can you play in Those Who Came?
Travel to different areas of Solarus to follow the storyline, or join the Arena to have fun competing against other Sainen explorers -- of course, in a friendly, non-combat way! Both game modes require more players to join forces with you, so these teammates will be chosen by the matchmaking system unless you invite your friends. And yes, that means that a stable internet connection is required to play Those Who Came.

How does the Arena work?
Explore the map in search of charged generators to extract energy for your headquarters as you try to sabotage your enemy’s supply before you run out of time.

Will you add more story chapters over the course of the Early Access period?
Yes. We’re still figuring out how to blend the narrative aspect of Those Who Came with its gameplay. It will take some time, but our plan consists in updating the game little by little with new missions, features, maps, and characters. Just wait and see!

How many friends can I invite to join my party?
In Solarus, you’ll recruit three companions to complete the story missions. At the Arena, up to eight players will be able to join you as allies or rivals in 2v2, 3v3, and 4v4 “battles”.

What do you do to protect players against toxic behaviors?
According to the essence of Those Who Came, we expect to minimize the possibility of getting exposed to toxic behaviors and build a comfortable space for all kinds of players. That’s the reason why we refused to include chat features. Players can interact by using animated emotes, and talk via third-party apps like Discord or Teamspeak.

Are you planning a single-player mode?
Those Who Came reaches its full potential as a multiplayer game, given that we decided to focus on cooperation as the best way to save Solarus -- but yes, the single-player mode is in our roadmap!



USER SUPPORT

Am I allowed to customize my keyboard shortcuts?
We’ll enable the option at some point in the Early Access phase.

Will the game support controllers?
It will!

Where can I report bugs?
In the game, press ESC to open the Home Menu and select the bug icon at the bottom right corner of the screen. It will take you to our official Support form, where you can send us a detailed explanation and attach a screenshot. Also, we usually read the discussions here on Steam, so feel free to share your issues. But if you need a quick response, we recommend you to join our official Discord server or contact us via Twitter -- our DMs are always open!

How long do I have to wait before the issue is solved?
Our support team checks their inbox and the Discord server on a daily basis. Since not all bugs are of equal severity, we ask for your patience while we look for the best way to deal with each problem. If a bug significantly disrupts the gameplay experience, it will be given the highest priority and we will proceed to fix it immediately.

Can I suggest new features too?
Of course! We’re always happy to read what players think about our work and how do they think it can be improved -- but please remember that we need a reasonable time to determine whether the suggested feature fits within our design and the objectives set for the game.

notes.title: Early Access release date announced!
notes.content:
EARLY ACCESS

“Those Who Came”, the adventurous sci-fi non-combat-based RPG, will be coming to Steam in Early Access, on October 7, 2021


[previewyoutube=TXN7oj6Fz4Q;full][/previewyoutube]

Presented publicly at Gamescom a few weeks ago, “Those who Came” is an immersive experience that will put your skills to the test and awaken your lateral thinking, where cooperation and teamwork are keys to evolving throughout the game.

In “Those Who Came”, your civilization has been forced into exodus and you just found Solarus. Choose your suits, mods, and gear up with extraordinary magic to change the world. Play as an airy, firei, ether, or jointer character as you explore the environment.
Add the game to your wishlist to receive more updates as well! 

See you all soon!

notes.title: Demo available until September 30!
notes.content:
THOSE WHO CAME GAME AVAILABLE 

The game is available on Steam till the end of September in tandem with the Gamescom event. The game is played solo, but for a fully immersive and maximum experience, it is best played as a group of 2 or 4. As they say, The more the merrier. #ItTakesFour

“Those Who Came” is an immersive experience that will put your skills to the test and awaken your lateral thinking, where cooperation and teamwork are keys to evolving throughout the game. Violence won’t make you win, your abilities will, that’s why lateral thinking is a must. 

 Being the first launch of  ROLLDBOX GAMES, “Those Who Came” brings us a fascinating story to play in a cooperative environment, giving you an enriching experience and learning from the power of the team. But above all, you will get a boost of positive energy that will leave you wanting more.

Gamescom is one of the most important conventions in the video game industry. A 100% virtual meeting that will bring together players from all over the world to celebrate the new titles and discover the latest market launches.

For this year’s Gamescom event, you will find “Those Who Came” in Floor 5 - RPG - booth 18 at the Indie Arena Booth-Arcade Village. 

Features
Choose your suits, mods 
Player versus Environment
Play as a team
Non combat-based RPG
